DMAdata_StBr2.name: Status bar: update counters and tiles
summary: Data first: DMA setup for status bar row 2 (source [$0F15], 27 bytes to VRAM), LUIGI name tiles, item box tile and palette tables, big bonus star digit tiles.
Code at $008E1A (called once per frame): runs the level timer (a tick every ~40 frames, hurry-up music at 099, KillMario at 000), clamps scores to 999,999,
builds the score, time, coin, lives and bonus star digit tiles in the row buffers [$0EF9] (row 1) and [$0F15] (row 2), adds pending coins
([$13CC]) one per frame with a 1-up at 100, starts the bonus game at 100 bonus stars, swaps MARIO for LUIGI and draws the item box and Yoshi coin icons.
The tiles are DMAed to VRAM by DrawStatusBar. Tile $FC is the blank tile used to hide leading zeros.

s008FFA.name: Table: powers of ten for decimal conversion
summary: Six 32-bit entries (high word, low word): 100,000, 10,000, 1,000, 100, 10, 1. Used with Y = 4 * entry by the routines at $009012 and $009051.

s009012.name: Convert 32-bit value to six decimal digit tiles
summary: Counts how many times each power of ten can be subtracted from the 32-bit value, one tile per digit (left to right).
Parameters: [$00]-[$01] high word, [$02]-[$03] low word of the value; X = offset into the tile buffer [$0F15]; Y = 0 (start at 100,000s).
Returns: digit tiles at [$0F15+X]...; the value variables are destroyed.

HexToDec.name: Hex to decimal and item box drawing
summary: $009045: converts A (0-99) to decimal by repeated subtraction. Returns: X = tens, A = ones.
$009051: 16-bit version of the routine above, used for the bonus star counter. Parameters: [$02] value, X = tile offset ([$0F15+X]), Y = 4 * first power of ten (Y = $10 gives two digits).
$009079: draws the item box sprite (reserve item [$0DC2]) at X = $78, Y = $0F as a 16x16 sprite; the star flashes through palettes. Hides OAM slot 0 in Mode 7 boss rooms.

s0090D1.name: Table: text sprite tiles, upper half
summary: Indexed by text column (CODE_0091E9). Probably the letters of the Mario Start! / bonus game messages; $FF = blank column.

s009105.name: Table: text sprite tiles, lower half
summary: Same indexes as DATA_0090D1; tile of the sprite drawn 8 pixels below the upper one.

s009139.name: Table: text sprite properties, upper half

s00916A.name: Table: text sprite properties, lower half
summary: Mostly the upper values with the Y flip bit set, so the lower sprite looks like a mirrored copy of the upper one (probably a reflection).

s00919B.name: Mario Start text and level setup helpers
summary: $00919B: during Mario animation $0A runs the Mario animation handler; otherwise sets [$0DC0] = $1E when [$141A] is 0 (purpose unclear).
$0091B1: draws the "Mario Start!" / "Luigi Start!" text (or the bonus game text when [$1425] is set, which also zeroes the timer) as 14 columns of two sprites.
$0091E9: draws one text column from the tables at $0090D1-$00916A at X position [$00] and steps [$00] left by 8.

NintenDMAINIT.name: Set CGRAM color 0 to black by DMA
summary: Clears the palette mirror word [$0703] and DMAs it into CGRAM color 0 with channel 2. Used at the Nintendo Presents screen and the ending.

s009249.name: Table: DMA setup for black backdrop

s009250.name: Init HDMA window effect (channel 7)
summary: Sets up HDMA channel 7 to write the window registers WH0/WH1 from an indirect table, disables all HDMA ([$0D9F] = 0) and fills the window table
at $04A0-$065F (224 lines of left, right) with left = $FF, right = $00 so no screen area is inside the window.
$009260 is the entry used to just disable HDMA, $009263 clears the table only.

s009277.name: HDMA setup and table: window effect

s009283.name: Window HDMA: enable fully covered window
summary: Clears the window table, then (unless [$0D9B] bit 0 is set) fills the last line with a window covering the whole line and enables channel 7.

WindowHDMAenable.name: Fill window table lines, set up scroll HDMA
summary: $009291: loop that writes left = $00, right = $FF entries from offset X upwards to the end of the window table, then enables HDMA channel 7 ([$0D9F] = $80).
$0092A8: clears the table and opens the last 20 lines through the loop above.
$0092B2: used in the ending (game mode $23). Sets up HDMA channels 5-7 to write BG1, BG2 and BG3 horizontal scroll per scanline from tables at $04A0, $04AA, $04B4
(10 bytes each: 88-line segments with the scroll words taken from [$1A], [$1E], [$22] and [$1462]...); enables channels 5-7 ([$0D9F] = $E0).

s009313.name: Table: HDMA setup for BG scroll channels
summary: Five bytes per channel (DMAP, B-bus, table address low and high, bank) for channels 5, 6 and 7.

GetGameMode.name: Run current game mode
summary: Jumps to the routine for the game mode in [$0100] using the pointer table that follows the JSL (ExecutePtr).

Ptrs009329.name: Pointer table: game modes
summary: One 16-bit pointer per game mode ($00-$29), indexed by [$0100]. Names inferred from the code; several are marked as uncertain.

TurnOffIO.name: Turn off NMI, IRQ, HDMA and screen
summary: NMITIMEN = 0, HDMA off, force blank. Called from the start of most game modes.

NintendoPos.name: Table: Nintendo logo sprite X positions

NintendoTile.name: Game mode 00: load Nintendo Presents
summary: First the logo tile table. Code: clears the screen, loads graphics and palette, builds four 16x16 logo sprites at Y = $70 (X from NintendoPos,
tiles from this table), starts the [$1DF5] timer at $40, sets full brightness, makes the backdrop black and moves on to game mode 01.

Mode04Finish.name: Enable NMI and joypad, return
summary: Reached by falling through from the game mode increment at $0093F4. Writes NMITIMEN = $81.

ScreenSettings.name: Set screen layers; game modes 01 and 06
summary: $0093FD: sets CGADSUB (A, also mirrored in [$40]), main screen layers (X), sub screen layers (Y) and clears the window mask designation. Returns.
$00940F (game mode 01): counts [$1DF5] down, then decompresses Mario graphics and goes to game mode 02.
$00941B (game mode 06): title screen circle effect. Each frame the circle size [$1433] grows by 4 until $F0 and is drawn into the window HDMA table (centre $80,$70);
pressing a button jumps to the final size $EC and finishes title screen setup.

CutsceneBgColor.name: Table: cutscene background settings
summary: Indexed by cutscene number - 1; value goes to [$192F] when a cutscene is loaded.
